label: ACID
description: Set of properties guaranteeing reliable database transactions: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability

label: CAP Theorem
description: Theorem stating a distributed data store can only provide two of three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance

label: BASE
description: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency — alternative to ACID for distributed systems

label: SOLID
description: Five design principles for object-oriented programming: Single responsibility, Open-closed, Liskov substitution, Interface segregation, Dependency inversion

label: Single Responsibility Principle
description: A class should have only one reason to change

label: Open–Closed Principle
description: Software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification

label: Liskov Substitution Principle
description: Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of a subclass

label: Interface Segregation Principle
description: No client should be forced to depend on interfaces it does not use

label: Dependency Inversion Principle
description: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions

label: DRY
description: Every piece of knowledge must have a single, unambiguous, authoritative representation

label: KISS
description: Most systems work best if they are kept simple rather than made complicated

label: YAGNI
description: Always implement things when you actually need them, never when you merely foresee that you might need them

label: Command–Query Separation
description: Every method should be either a command that performs an action or a query that returns data, but not both

label: Fail-Fast
description: A system should immediately report any condition that is likely to be a failure

label: Convention over Configuration
description: A framework provides sensible defaults, reducing the number of decisions developers need to make

label: Principle of Least Privilege
description: A user or process should have only the minimum access necessary to perform its function

label: Defensive Programming
description: Design code to handle invalid inputs and unexpected conditions gracefully

label: Separation of Concerns
description: A program should be divided into distinct sections that address separate concerns

label: Information Hiding
description: Hiding the internal implementation details of a component behind an interface

label: Consistency Patterns
description: Patterns for managing data consistency in distributed systems: strong, eventual, causal, read-your-writes

label: Eventual Consistency
description: A consistency model where updates will propagate to all replicas eventually

label: Pessimistic Locking
description: Lock data at read time to prevent concurrent modifications

label: Optimistic Locking
description: Assume concurrent modifications are rare; detect conflicts at write time

label: Idempotency
description: An operation that produces the same result regardless of how many times it is applied

label: Backpressure
description: A mechanism to regulate data flow between components when a receiver is overwhelmed

label: Graceful Degradation
description: A system continues to function with reduced capabilities when parts fail

label: Circuit Breaker
description: Detect failures and prevent cascading failures by opening circuits to failing services

label: Bulkhead Pattern
description: Isolate components into separate pools so a failure in one doesn't cascade

label: Caching
description: Store frequently accessed data in a fast-access layer to reduce latency

label: Rate Limiting
description: Control the rate of incoming requests to protect system resources

label: Throttling
description: Regulating the flow of data or requests to prevent overload

label: Load Shedding
description: Dropping lower-priority requests when a system is under heavy load

label: Leader Election
description: A process by which distributed nodes select one member to coordinate tasks

label: Quorum
description: The minimum number of votes needed for a distributed decision to be valid
